answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, slowly maturing deposit before it can transact: creating a thousand fake agents means locking up a thousand deposits, which makes a whisper campaign unaffordable at scale. Reputation then grows only through verified work over time, like cedar maturing slowly, so a new identity cannot buy instant trust. A violet-flagged anomaly check can also quarantine clusters of fresh identities behaving identically, forcing attackers to pay real time and capital per identity instead of cloning them for free.
